chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from some of his companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
He said to me: “The prayer of the day is sixteen rakʿahs; whichever part of the day you wish—if you wish, in its beginning; and if you wish, in its middle; and if you wish, in its end.”

key_terms.آخِرِهِ: the end portion of the day
key_terms.النَّهَارِ: the daytime period in which this prayer is performed
key_terms.سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ: the number sixteen, specifying the total rakʿahs
key_terms.صَلَاةُ: the prescribed prayer being discussed in this report
key_terms.وَسَطِهِ: the middle portion of the day

ai.seo_question: How many rakʿahs are in the daytime prayer, and when can they be performed?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the daytime prayer consists of sixteen rakʿahs and allows flexibility in performing them during the day. It indicates a legislated devotional practice whose timing within the daytime period is open to the worshipper.
